text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.52% today to $422.33, extending a sharp rally that began October 1st—the stock jumped nearly 7% in two days. The driver appears to be the widening gap between U.S. and world oil prices: crude is trading at $96/barrel domestically but $114 globally, a $18 spread that has grown as geopolitical tensions escalate (U.S. military buildup in the Middle East, threats toward Iran) and the G7 announced a 100-million-barrel reserve release over four months. For a refiner, a wider U.S.-global price gap can be profitable if it means cheaper feedstock at home while international demand and pricing remain elevated.

The rally also reflects tightening fundamentals despite the reserve release. Refineries are running at 92.5% capacity with diesel storage notably lean at 105 million barrels—and the news highlights acute diesel shortages in Europe and supply constraints from Middle East instability. This supports margins for U.S. refiners even as the G7's move aims to ease global pressure on fuel prices.
